records.name: ITAV Foundation
records.summary: A volunteer-run nonprofit that supports Philadelphia families with a diaper bank, maternal support and education, and a skin care program. It also serves Jamaica.
records.what_you_do: Call or email the group to ask about volunteering at the diaper bank, becoming a vendor, or joining an upcoming event. Donations go through its PayPal link.

first_step.how: Call 215-512-6465 or email info@itavf.org to ask about volunteering at the diaper bank or joining an upcoming event.
first_step.basis: The contact page gives a phone number and email for questions, but it does not describe volunteer openings, diaper bank hours or event dates.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a volunteer shift, diaper bank hours or event days. The one step it gives is to call or email with questions.
first_visit_tips: Call before you come, since the site lists no office hours or diaper bank days.

records.notes: Deep pass. The home page returned only its title. The volunteer, events, upcoming-events and diaper-bank paths returned not found. The contact page names a Diaper Bank and an Upcoming Events menu item but gives no details on either. The copyright range ending in 2026 is not used as evidence, and no dated items were found. A media contact on the contact page is not recorded.

records.name: Jesus Christ in Power Ministries
records.summary: A congregation with Sunday school, Sunday worship, and weeknight services. It says everyone is welcome, including people who do not have a church home.
records.what_you_do: Attend a Sunday or weeknight service, join Sunday school, or send a prayer request through the form on the website. The community programs page also lists a Friday 11 am to 1 pm slot, a first-Friday 9 to 11 am slot, and named programs (Kiddie Carnival, Community Prayer Walk, Men 4 the Master and Work Crew) with no details on any of them.

schedule.text: Sunday school at 10 am (April to September) or 11 am (October to March). Sunday service at 11 am (April to September) or 12 pm (October to March). Weeknight services on Wednesday at 7:30 pm, Thursday at 7 pm, and Friday at 6 pm. Communion is the first Sunday of each month.

cost.text: The site lists no fee. It accepts donations through a Cash App link.

access.notes: Services can also be joined by conference phone line, (508) 924-2249, as the home page lists.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday or weeknight service, or call (267) 297-7179 or email info@JesusnPowerMin.org to ask about times.
first_step.basis: The site says visitors are welcome even without a church home and lists the service times. It does not describe a separate newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Services run Sunday mornings and on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday evenings, and Sunday school comes before the Sunday service. The site does not say how long a service lasts, what language it uses, or what the service feels like. You can ask anyone at the ministry for prayer or a listening ear, and no fee is listed.
first_visit_tips: Check which season's start time applies, since the page lists different times for April to September and October to March.
The site gives no parking or transit details, so call ahead for directions.

records.notes: Deep pass: home page, community programs and pastors pages were read, and the conference line was checked on a second read of the home page. The community programs page gives no details for its named programs and lists no dated events. The pastors page says the ministry helps with a weekly food distribution, but gives no days or hours, so it is not in the schedule. No pages give language, parking or wheelchair details. Tier 1 said the site lists no volunteer program. The community programs page names a Work Crew, with no details, so that statement is corrected in what_you_do.

records.name: Kindred 360
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs virtual peer support groups and webinars for Black parents and caregivers. Its free Changemaker membership adds on-demand wellness content, such as movement sessions and recipes.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a virtual support group through its Join Us link (most groups are marked coming soon), or join the free Changemaker membership for on-demand content. You can also email changemaker@kindred360.org to ask when a group opens.

schedule.text: Virtual peer support groups and webinars held on Zoom. Most groups are marked coming soon, with no set day or time yet.

cost.text: The Changemaker membership is free. The page states no fee for support groups, and it describes the P.I.E.S. workshop as free.

first_step.how: Pick a group and use its Join Us link to register on Zoom. For the online library, sign up for the free Changemaker membership.
first_step.basis: Sign-up is free and clearly marked, and the groups are open to parents and caregivers. The page limits the resources to Black parents, and most groups are still coming soon.
first_step.what_to_expect: Support groups are peer groups held on Zoom, led by hosts who are not licensed therapists and who do not replace professional care. The page does not say how long a session lasts or how many people attend. Most groups are marked coming soon, so a group may not be open to join yet.
first_visit_tips: Confirm which group you are registering for, since the page notes that the High-Risk Pregnancy link goes to the same Zoom page as NICU Parents.
Have a device ready with audio and video, since the groups meet on Zoom.

records.notes: Deep pass. The support groups page lists ten groups. All but one are marked coming soon. The Doulas and Birth Workers session on October 28, 2026 at 7 pm (the page says EST) is the only dated item, and it is used only for last_sign_of_life. That group is for doulas and birth workers, not parents. The page says the hosts are not licensed therapists and points to 988 for crisis support. The Oxygen Self-Care and Wellness page says the resources are offered exclusively to Black parents. Tier 1 had the Broad Street address twice, so the duplicate is dropped. Two separate reads reported that the newsletter form shows a site error (a message that it needs a storage option). That was not tested directly, so the record makes no claim about it. The Facebook group was not fetched.

records.name: Know Your Worth Girls Inc
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that works with girls ages 8 to 17 on mentoring, money skills and wellness. It holds public events such as skate nights, money workshops and pop-ups.
records.what_you_do: Come to a public event such as a family skate night, a money skills workshop or a pop-up. Ask by email about mentoring, and use the Subscribe option on the Zeffy page to get event notices.

schedule.text: Several public events a year, such as a family skate night, money skills workshops and pop-up events. Dates are posted on the Zeffy page.

locations.label: Family skate night venue (Rolling Thunder Skate Center)

first_step.how: Email knowyourworthgirlsinc@gmail.com about mentoring, or use the Subscribe button on the group's Zeffy page to get notice of the next event and buy tickets through that event's link.
first_step.basis: Public events list dates and places with ticket links, and a Subscribe button sends event notices. The page does not say how mentoring places are filled.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public events include family skate nights, money skills workshops and pop-ups, and most listings give a date, time and place. The page does not say what tickets cost, so check the event link before you go. Mentoring is described only in general terms, so ask by email how it works.
first_visit_tips: The program serves girls ages 8 to 17, so check who an event is for before you sign up a child.
Use the link on each event page for tickets and registration.

records.notes: Deep pass. The group's own site returned a redirect loop on the home address, a TLS handshake error on the www address, and not found for /programs, /about and /get-involved, so the Zeffy event list was the main source. Events with the year written in the listing: a 2026 family skate night (Jan 15), a 2026 Black Girls Art Show (Mar 28) and Philly Muslim Girls Empowerment Day 2026 (Apr 5). Undated listings are not used as evidence. Some money workshops are run with Chase, per the event titles. A fish fry fundraiser listing names Parkside Association of Philadelphia, with no link, so it is not checked. Ticket prices are not stated.

records.name: LUCKY Youth Program
records.summary: A youth organization that pairs young people with mentors for school, leadership and career planning. It also offers educational opportunities, arts and culture activities, and trips.
records.what_you_do: Families can email mentoring@luckymp.org with the subject 'Mentoring Request' to ask for a mentor. People who want to help can email development@luckymp.org with the subject 'Volunteer Opportunities', and volunteers upload child abuse and criminal clearances on the Volunteer Corner page. Mentoring tracks cover leadership, academics and career planning.

schedule.text: Mentoring runs monthly or weekly, according to the group's site. The site lists no set days or times.

locations.label: Service areas named on the About page
locations.neighborhood: Germantown, North Philadelphia, Kensington and East Falls

cost.text: The site lists no fee for families or volunteers.

first_step.how: Families: email mentoring@luckymp.org with the subject 'Mentoring Request'. Volunteers: email development@luckymp.org, and upload your child abuse and criminal clearances on the Volunteer Corner page.
first_step.basis: Families can email to request a mentor, but the site does not explain intake or matching. Volunteers are asked to upload child abuse and criminal clearances.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a mentoring session or how often a mentor and young person meet. It says mentoring is offered monthly and weekly, and names service areas in Germantown, North Philadelphia, Kensington and East Falls. Families start by emailing the mentoring address, and the site lists no fee for families or volunteers.
first_visit_tips: Check the age track first: leadership and academic mentoring is for ages 5 to 15, and career path mentoring is for ages 16 to 24.
Volunteers should expect to upload child abuse and criminal clearances.

records.notes: Deep pass. The Volunteer Corner page asks volunteers to upload child abuse and criminal clearances, recorded as act153_clearances and background_check. Age tracks come from the home page. The About page names service areas but no street addresses. The Connect with us page is a coming soon placeholder. The awards item (June 8th, no year) is not used as evidence. The /lucky-mentoring and /mentoring pages returned not found, so the only intake route is the email request.

records.name: Pamper and Diaper My Baby
records.summary: A nonprofit that stocks diapers and passes them to partner charities that work with families facing emergencies. It runs diaper drives and volunteer work to keep supplies coming.
records.what_you_do: Ask about Heart 2 Heart volunteering through the Contact Us page, join a diaper drive, or follow the group's Instagram for pop-up events. Diapers go only to partner nonprofits, not to individual families, so a family in need cannot request diapers here directly.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page at padmb.org/contact-us, or email padmbitems@gmail.com, to ask how to join Heart 2 Heart volunteering or a diaper drive.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says to contact the group to sign up. It does not say what volunteers do, when help is needed, or whether drives are open to the public.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe what a volunteer does on a shift or how long it takes. Drives and pop-up events are announced on social media, and the events page lists no dated events right now.
first_visit_tips: Follow the group's Instagram for pop-up dates, since the events page points there.
If you give items and want a tax receipt, use the contact form and name the items you donated.

records.notes: Deep pass. The Heart 2 Heart page is a recruiting notice for volunteers at 2025 events, with no month. It is not used for last_sign_of_life, because that field needs a month. The events page names no drives, dates or places and points to social media. The Contact Us page lists padmbitems@gmail.com, which is added to contacts. It lists no phone number or street address. Not stated anywhere: whether drives are open to the public, what volunteers do, time commitment, age or background check rules, languages, or accessibility.

records.name: Philadelphia Freedom Schools
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs summer reading and math programs where college and high school students teach younger students, with family and community involvement.
records.what_you_do: Use the Get Involved page to ask about summer teaching or volunteer roles. The school hires and trains high school students as Junior Servant Leaders, who get mentorship and training. Community partners and educators can use the same page to get involved.

schedule.text: Summer reading and math programs for K to 8 scholars, taught by high school and college-age students who prepare beforehand.

cost.text: The site lists no participant fee and asks for donations.

first_step.how: Open the Get Involved page at philadelphiafreedomschools.org and follow the volunteer or partner route, or sign up for the newsletter to get news and updates.
first_step.basis: The Get Involved page invites volunteers, partners and educators, but the FAQ and events pages give no steps, dates or requirements, and the events page says no events are scheduled.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a summer day, a teaching role or the hours involved. Junior Servant Leaders get training and mentorship from the school, and the events page says no events are scheduled right now.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the newsletter, since the site posts no dates for upcoming programs.
Ask the school directly what teachers and volunteers need, since the site does not list requirements.

records.notes: Deep pass: most inner pages are thin. The FAQ lists two addresses and no answers, and both differ from the IRS address, so all three are listed as published. The events page lists no upcoming events and no dated items, only a photo gallery of the most recent gathering. The accessibility statement is an unfinished template with placeholder contact details, so no access facts are recorded. The 25th anniversary celebration on December 14, 2024 is the newest dated item, and it sets last_sign_of_life. A web search for 2026 summer programs found nothing for this group. Its results covered a similarly named Freedom Schools Literacy Academy run by another Philadelphia nonprofit, and programs in other cities. None of that is recorded here. Confidence stays low.

notes: Searches: 1 of 1 used. It found no 2026 information for Philadelphia Freedom Schools, and one result carried an embedded line telling the reader how to cite sources. That line was ignored, and no search facts were recorded. Fetches: 35 in total, within the 6 per group limit for every group. No page returned a 403 or bot check, so blocked is empty. Several own-site paths returned 404 and are listed per group. The Know Your Worth home page returned a redirect loop and its www address a TLS handshake error. ITAV's home page returned only its title. Budget was not exhausted. All seven groups are verdict publish. No leads_only entries: no partner group with its own usable link was named on a group site. Parkside Association of Philadelphia is named on the Know Your Worth Zeffy page with no link and is mentioned in that record's notes.
